newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas pares losses late, still ends down.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas pares losses late, still ends down.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared losses late Friday but still ended lower across the board in moderate trade, lifted by some pre-weekend short covering after a sharp, two-day slide, industry sources said.
February finished 8.4 cents lower at $3.257 per million British thermal units after diving earlier to $3.08. March settled five cents lower at $2.859. Others also ended down.

"I think we saw some late short covering, people taking profits ahead of the weekend, but next week, it all depends on weather," said one Houston-based trader, adding it was still early in winter to see prices collapse.

While some said the prospect for another Arctic wave late next week could temper the bears Monday, others said balmy weather in Texas and the southern plains could trigger another test of psychological support at $3.00.
Technically, traders now pegged February support at Friday's low of $3.08, with support below $3.00 likely at the Dec 31 low of $2.613. Resistance was seen at $3.64 and then in the $3.80-3.84 area.

In the cash, weekend Gulf Coast prices tumbled about 80 cents to the $3.80s. Midcon pipes cratered more than $1.25 to the $3.50s and $3.60s. Cold weather hitting the East held New York city gate gas prices relatively steady at about $6.00.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell by 4.1 cents to $2.395. NYMEX said an estimated 44,426 Hub contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 40,189.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Friday.

On the KCBT, February closed five cents lower at $3.10, while deferreds finished down by one to three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.4 cents to 15.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 404 contracts traded, up from Thursday's total of 337.
